348179.statement:
Let $g,k$ be nonnegative integers and $N$ an integer, and consider the positive linear recurrence sequences associated with the coefficient lists

$$
[\underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{g},\underbrace{0,\dots,0}_{k},N]
\quad\text{and}\quad
[\underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{g+1},\underbrace{0,\dots,0}_{k},N].
$$

**Monotonicity conjecture.** If the sequence generated by $[\underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{g},\underbrace{0,\dots,0}_{k},N]$ is complete, then so is the sequence generated by $[\underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{g+1},\underbrace{0,\dots,0}_{k},N]$. The authors motivate this from observed numerical behavior: for fixed $k$, the maximal admissible $N$ increases with $g$ and eventually becomes constant. A general proof remains open.
